questions.q: Why does this capstone specifically call for three sources of different shapes (SQL Server export, CSV, JSON feed)?
options: Because the loading and transformation decisions genuinely change per source type, and practicing that matters more than the specific data used
Because Snowflake cannot load more than one file format per account
Because JSON and CSV cannot both be staged in the same schema
Because SQL Server exports must always be loaded before any other source
questions.explain: The point is practicing different loading/transform approaches (COPY INTO vs. VARIANT/FLATTEN, etc.), not repeating the same technique three times on similar data.

questions.q: According to the brief, what should the JSON source specifically require, to be a meaningful part of this capstone?
options: It should be nested enough to actually require VARIANT and FLATTEN, not secretly flat data in a JSON wrapper
It must be converted to CSV before loading
It must come from a Snowpipe-only source
It cannot contain more than 10 rows
questions.explain: A flat JSON file wouldn't exercise the semi-structured data skills from Chapter 7 — the brief calls for genuinely nested data.

questions.q: What is the recommended order of operations for this capstone, according to this lesson?
options: Load all three sources first, get the dimensional model correct, add RBAC once the structure is stable, then tune and connect Power BI last
Connect Power BI first, then figure out what data to load
Configure RBAC before any tables exist
Add Streams and Tasks before loading any data
questions.explain: The lesson argues you can't model what you haven't landed, shouldn't automate an unstable model, and shouldn't grant privileges on objects about to be restructured — so this order minimizes wasted work.

questions.q: What does "done" mean for this capstone, according to the lesson?
options: A stranger could open the reporting schema and understand the pattern from the objects themselves, without verbal explanation
You ran every step once, regardless of whether it still works
The project uses only the exact same dataset as Lesson 1's pilot lesson
Power BI is connected, with no requirement for RBAC or performance tuning
questions.explain: The bar is that the Snowflake objects themselves demonstrate the full pattern — loading, modeling, RBAC, and performance — not just that each step was performed once.

questions.q: Which two roles does the RBAC deliverable specifically call for at minimum?
options: A loader role and a read-only analyst role, with grants reflecting least privilege
Only ACCOUNTADMIN, used for everything
A Power BI service role and nothing else
One shared role used by every part of the pipeline
questions.explain: The brief calls for at least two roles with least-privilege grants — e.g. a loader role and a read-only analyst role — rather than everyone running as ACCOUNTADMIN.
